$comment: Every absolute http(s) origin that may appear anywhere in the production web build that
the offline APK bundles. audit-offline-web-assets.mjs fails the offline build on any origin
that is not listed here, so adding a runtime CDN, a web font, an analytics beacon or a
remote API to the webapp cannot reach the offline APK without someone deliberately writing
it down in this file - at which point the reason field is where they have to justify it.
Being listed here does NOT mean the URL is fetched. Almost none of these are: they are XML
namespaces, error-message links baked into libraries, and scam websites that CIBAR renders
as text because inventing them is the point of the exercise. What the list asserts is that
somebody looked at each one and established that it is not a network dependency.
The offline APK also declares no INTERNET permission (app/src/offline/AndroidManifest.xml),
so a URL that slipped past this audit still could not be fetched. This list is the check
that fails at build time, in CI, with a name and a line number - rather than on a phone in
aeroplane mode in front of an audience.

origins.reason: XML/SVG/XHTML namespace identifiers (xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"). Namespace URIs are names, not addresses; nothing ever resolves them.
react-router's internal placeholder base for parsing relative URLs when window.location has an opaque origin. Never navigated to.
Text inside @tensorflow/tfjs error messages ("file an issue at ...", "install our node backend, visit ...").
React's own error-message links, printed to the console when a React invariant fires.
react-router's error and deprecation message links.
react-i18next's useSuspense warning links to its own documentation.
MDN link inside an i18next error message about the fetch API signature.
Paper citations in @tensorflow/tfjs kernel source comments.
Attribution comment in a @tensorflow/tfjs WebGL shader.

lightweight-charts builds its required attribution <a> element with this href. It is a link the user may see on the GuGo Invest chart, not a resource the page loads; offline it simply cannot be followed, exactly like every other outbound link.

A fictional scam site. Scenario 01 renders the string as the fake investment platform's address - inventing a convincing fake URL is the teaching content. The domain is not owned by us and is never requested.

The first half of a fictional police case-verification URL (https://case-verify-<caseNumber>.sim-example.tw), assembled in Scenario 03's markup around the generated case number and shown as text. sim-example.tw is a reserved example domain.
The offline APK's own local origin (WebViewAssetLoader). The only entry here that is actually served - by OfflineWebAssetHandler, out of the APK's assets, with no socket involved.
